Theme

Tools, fasteners & household repair · Household, washing & chores

install verb

put in a machine or fitting

also fit, put in, have installed, installation

classical

Cic. Sest. 83: in rōstrīs collocātī (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 3.1 (Lewis & Short)

collocō, collocāre, collocāvī, collocātum

verb, first conjugation

place, set up, put in its place

The general verb for putting a thing where it is to stay: in eō locō collocāre. Also of people: to station troops, or to give a daughter in marriage (fīliam collocāre).

Other words

  • pōnō, pōnere, posuī, positum — put, set up

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical

    The plainest word, enough when the place is clear.

  • īnstruō, īnstruere, īnstrūxī, īnstrūctum — fit out, equip (a room, a house)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 333

    Of fitting out a place with what it needs rather than putting one thing in: domum īnstruere (Cic. Verr. 2.4.9). For software, see install.

Examples

  • Crās plumbārius veniet ut māchinam lavātōriam collocet.

    The plumber is coming tomorrow to install the washing machine.composed

See also install, washing machine, dishwasher, plumber, tool.

SourcesLewis & Short: colloco · Lewis & Short: pono · Lewis & Short: instruo

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 333.
